payload.name: Cognitive Drift
payload.fact: Cognitive Drift is a phenomenon where systems gradually lose context, grounding, or semantic fidelity while remaining functional.
payload.boundary: The process occurs in mediated systems where external tools and AI participate in memory and reasoning.

decision_note: DOMAIN_CONTAMINATION, delegated by owner. All four claims come from one source, DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.33000278.v1 — a self-published Figshare collection titled Cognition in Mediated Systems: AI Memory, External Thought, Decision Fatigue, and Co-Cognition. The owner held Memory Drift pending one question: does the source study human memory or machine systems? It studies machine systems. The term comes from the collection paper Persistent AI Memory and the Extended Architecture of Human Thought, which concerns long-context AI, persistent memory stores and AI assistants; the proposal boundary says so itself — occurs within mediated systems involving AI and external cognitive tools — and its fact names the subject as systems that participate in memory and reasoning. That is not a claim about a person. The rejection is source-level, so all four go together rather than one at a time. Recorded honestly: of the four, constraint-collapse does have a human subject and a product-relevant variable (weakening defaults transfers coordination work onto individuals). It falls here anyway because its source is the same non-peer-reviewed essay collection, which the pipeline graded A at confidence 0.95 and which measured nothing. A defaults claim worth keeping should re-enter from a source that measured one. How the DOI passed relevance selection, two answers. First, recordRelevanceTier is a bag-of-tokens gate: CL-14 evidence_terms tokenise to cognitive, load, working, memory, extraneous, split, attention, information, processing; the title supplies memory and the abstract supplies four more, which scores tier 1 — the top tier, ranked ahead of genuine cognitive-load papers. The gate never asks who the study is about. Second and blunter, the run manifest for github-actions-30818192427 records records_skipped_irrelevant 0 against records_processed 293: the gate rejected nothing at all on that run, as on 19 of the 20 runs in run_history. The relevance pre-filter is not currently filtering.
